newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end moderately higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end moderately higher.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed moderately higher after the U.S. Federal Reserve ended its meeting Tuesday without changing rates, and also helped by a rise in Wall Street's and Brady Bonds prices, dealers said.
"We saw a firm market today in spite of the U.S. long bond rate movements," a broker at a huge local bank said. The long bond rate rose to 6.69 percent before closing at 6.66.
He added Argentine Bradies were up, mostly FRBs, which rose 3/16 to close at $85-3/4. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 gained 0.12 percent to end at 122.25.
The broker said those bonds may be nearing their ceiling.
The Bocon Previsional 3, denominated in pesos, rose a strong 0.45 percent to 89.20 although with little liquidity.
Volume also rose and many buy orders emerged in the local market around 1915 GMT after, as was widely expected, the Fed ended its meeting without changing rates.
Dealers said the Argentine bond market was also upheld by a rise in the Dow Jones, that closed up 0.64 percent at 6.308,33.
